quickAnswerTitle: Minnesota School Calendar Dates Are Local — and 2026–27 Has a Special Start Rule
quickAnswer: Minnesota does not publish one statewide K–12 calendar. For 2026–27 and 2027–28, a temporary state provision lets a school board vote to begin on September 1 or later even when Labor Day falls later. Four reviewed Twin Cities districts begin their main student schedules September 8, 2026; District 196 begins August 31 and then closes September 4 and 7. Because that date is earlier than September 1, the temporary provision alone does not explain it.
about:
Minnesota school calendars are adopted locally, not issued as one statewide student schedule. The reviewed Twin Cities calendars share some recognizable dates—especially MEA Break—but differ on first days by grade, conference closures, staff planning days, religious observances, grading periods, translated resources, and the last student day.

The start of 2026–27 is unusually important. Minnesota's standing calendar statute generally keeps elementary and secondary school from starting before Labor Day unless an exception applies. A temporary provision for 2026–27 and 2027–28 lets school boards vote to start September 1 or later. Anoka-Hennepin, Minneapolis, Osseo, and Saint Paul place their main openings after Labor Day on September 8, 2026. District 196 starts all students August 31 and closes September 4 and 7. That date is earlier than the temporary September 1 authority, so this page does not infer the district's legal basis from the calendar PDF alone.

The districtwide calendar is only the planning baseline. Minneapolis and Saint Paul stagger Pre-K and kindergarten, Anoka-Hennepin uses grade-specific openings and kindergarten Welcome Week, several districts use grade-band conference closures, and Eastview High School in District 196 follows quarters while most of that district follows trimesters. Families should pair the district calendar with the assigned school's bell schedule, program calendar, transportation notices, and weather updates.
calendarRulesDescription: Minnesota law sets calendar boundaries and minimum instruction, while local boards decide the actual attendance dates and grade-level details.

calendarRules.label: Temporary September 1 start authority
calendarRules.description: For 2026–27 and 2027–28 only, Minnesota districts may vote to start September 1 or later instead of waiting until after Labor Day. Earlier dates still require another statutory exception.

calendarRules.label: Minimum instructional days and hours
calendarRules.description: The annual calendar must include at least 165 instructional days for grades 1–11 unless an approved four-day week applies. State law also sets grade-band hour minimums.

calendarRules.label: Up to five weather e-learning days
calendarRules.description: A district with an adopted plan may use up to five e-learning days for inclement weather. These count as instructional days and are not the same as a full no-school closure.

calendarRules.label: Religious and American Indian cultural accommodation
calendarRules.description: Minnesota districts must make reasonable efforts to accommodate students excused from curricular activities for religious observances or American Indian cultural practices, observances, or ceremonies.

calendarRules.label: Grade and program calendars can diverge
calendarRules.description: Pre-K, kindergarten, high school conferences, alternative programs, digital-day rotations, and school-specific schedules may not follow every date on the general K–12 calendar.

stateSections.label: Five Reviewed Districts, Three Opening Patterns
stateSections.content: The date stored as a district's first day does not always mean every student begins then. Minneapolis and Saint Paul delay Pre-K and kindergarten; Anoka-Hennepin splits the opening by grade and uses kindergarten Welcome Week; District 196 starts all students together before Labor Day.

stateSections.label: MEA Is Shared; Winter and Spring Breaks Are Not
stateSections.content: All five reviewed calendars close for MEA October 15–16, 2026. The longer breaks split into different patterns, so a shared metro area does not guarantee matching child-care or travel dates.

planningTips: Do not infer a child's first day from the statewide start rule. Check the district and grade because Pre-K, kindergarten, transition grades, and other students may begin on different dates.
Treat MEA Break as a useful comparison point, not proof that the rest of two districts' calendars match.
Check the grade range on conference and staff-planning dates. Some Minnesota calendars close only elementary, K–8, PreK–5, or grades 9–12.
A declared e-learning day is an instructional day, while a weather closure may still become a makeup day or change the last day of school.
Use translated calendars as access resources, but check the current English master when versions disagree and review the district page's disclosed source notes.

faqs.q: Are Minnesota school calendars the same statewide?
faqs.a: No. Minnesota law establishes boundaries and instructional minimums, but local school boards adopt district calendars. First days, grade-specific openings, breaks, conferences, staff days, and last days differ.

faqs.q: Can Minnesota schools start before Labor Day in 2026?
faqs.a: For 2026–27 and 2027–28, a temporary provision allows a school board to vote to begin September 1 or later. A start earlier than September 1 still requires another applicable exception under Minnesota law.

faqs.q: When is Minnesota MEA Break in 2026?
faqs.a: All five reviewed district calendars list no school October 15–16, 2026, for MEA Break or MEA. Families should still verify their own district, school, and program calendar.

faqs.q: How many school days are required in Minnesota?
faqs.a: Minnesota's annual calendar must include at least 165 instructional days for students in grades 1–11 unless the commissioner has approved a four-day week. The law also sets instructional-hour minimums by grade band.

faqs.q: How many e-learning days can Minnesota schools use for weather?
faqs.a: A Minnesota district or charter school with a qualifying plan may use up to five inclement-weather e-learning days in one school year. They count as instructional days.

faqs.q: Do Minnesota kindergarten students start on the district's first day?
faqs.a: Not always. Minneapolis and Saint Paul start Pre-K and kindergarten after grades 1–12, while Anoka-Hennepin uses school-specific kindergarten Welcome Week. District 196 lists one opening for all students.

faqs.q: Do Twin Cities districts have the same Spring Break?
faqs.a: No. In the reviewed 2026–27 calendars, Anoka-Hennepin, Osseo, and District 196 use March 29–April 2, while Minneapolis and Saint Paul use April 5–9.

faqs.q: Can I add a Minnesota school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed district pages provide an ICS file that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. It is a one-time import and will not automatically receive later district revisions.
